description: Follow-up to op-hzs.32. The centroid-subdivision tetrahedralize (src/tet.rs) is space-filling and volume-conserving but NOT quality-optimised (24 tets/hex, no shape guarantee beyond positive volume on convex cells). Add Delaunay-quality refinement: edge/face flips toward the Delaunay criterion + sliver removal + size/quality-driven point insertion (Delaunay refinement). Reference-clean sources: gmsh (GPLv2+, GPLv3-compatible — its own Delaunay/frontal meshers only, NOT contrib/TetGen which is AGPL), cfMesh, Cheng/Dey/Shewchuk 'Delaunay Mesh Generation'. V&V: min dihedral angle / radius-edge ratio improves vs raw centroid tets; volume still conserved; boundary still conforms.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: Increment 1 landed (commit 834b739): smart-Laplacian smoothing (src/smooth.rs) — laplacian_smooth(&VolumeMesh, passes). Interior vertices relax to neighbour centroid only if no incident cell inverts (Freitag smart smoothing); boundary pinned so topology + total volume preserved exactly. V&V: perturbed tet quality recovered, 0 inversions, volume conserved, boundary bbox unchanged. REMAINING on this bead: flip-based Delaunay optimisation (2-3/3-2 flips toward in-sphere criterion) + sliver removal + size-driven point insertion. gmsh (GPLv2+, GPLv3-compatible — own Delaunay meshers only, NOT contrib/TetGen) is the licence-clean reference.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: Increment 2 landed (commit cb39132): flip-based Delaunay (src/delaunay.rs) — flip_to_delaunay via bistellar 2->3/3->2 flips + Shewchuk orient3d/insphere predicates (f64). Sweep-based tombstoned driver (fast, bounded). Robustness: refuses invalid input (negative-vol cells -> returned unchanged), 2x growth cap, and an improve-or-noop meta-guard so it can NEVER make a mesh worse. V&V (4 tests+doctest): non-Delaunay bipyramid -> Delaunay via one 2->3 flip; hex-block tet mesh flip conserves volume + valid + bounded growth + no worse; tangled 22k-tet snapped mesh returns unchanged in ~8ms (was: naive driver exploded to 111k). REMAINING: exact/adaptive predicates (robustness on near-degenerate configs) + size-driven point insertion (Bowyer-Watson) to reach GLOBAL Delaunay, not just local optimum.

title: cfmesh: Delaunay-quality tet refinement (improve tet shape/count)

design:
Child epic of the nuclear refinery programme (bn op-upme).

**Fidelity target: Crude estimate initially**

**Keep this modular. Do not choose one capture route globally yet.**

Potential sources: FCC regenerator; hydrogen/syngas processes; Claus/offgas;
auxiliary combustion; coke conversion.

Candidate routes discussed: alkanolamine; carbonate/bicarbonate; promoted MgO;
calcium looping. **Model the interface, not a committed choice.**

Streams should make concentrated CO2 available for compression, geological
storage, utilization, and syngas/CO/methanol pathways later.

## Ledger requirement

**Track compression electricity separately from thermal regeneration duty.**
They are different utilities with different sources -- conflating them destroys
the argument for using nuclear heat, since one is work and one is heat.

## Out of scope for this pass (programme-wide)

Do not: port DWSIM UI or graphical flowsheet objects; port CAPE-OPEN unless a
concrete backend requirement exists; reproduce .NET class architecture; make
DWSIM depend on Outram-FOAM; solve thousands of molecular species in the CDU;
implement molecular reconstruction before assay/pseudocomponent CDU works; call
a converged model validated without reference evidence; hide conservation
errors; push to `main`.
title: Refinery: CO2 capture / CCS / CCU interface
